acceptance: The fast-forward check before the repo-contract scan is read-only: rev-list / diff --cached / a branch-ahead probe only — no stageForLanding, no inbox consumption, no ship.lock, no worktree or index change before verifyAuditBinding
A test proves an edits-only diverged fleet lane leaves the inbox, the index and the worktree untouched before verifyAuditBinding
It saves a scan for the lane shape ship actually sees (core resets the lane to its base after build: HEAD == base with staged edits), or the plan records why S1 stays dropped

consumed.resolution: SUPERSEDED: acceptance 3 alternative met; docs/plans/fleet-landing-at-scale-2026-10.md:315 records 'S1 stays dropped' with its reasons (cycle 1960, 39f4c93e5); S5 and S6 save the scan instead. Triage 2026-10-20, verified twice.

fix: Redesign S1 as a pure probe: decide divergence from main vs the base the pending commit will have (HEAD) without staging; or drop S1 and rely on S5/S6.
source: landing plan S1 lane, review rounds 1-2 (2026-10-13)
summary: Landing plan S1 (fast-forward check before the scan) is deferred after two review rounds. Round 1: an early return left the lane uncommitted, so the recovery classified it as already landed and dropped the work. Round 2: the safe version (only committed+clean lanes) staged the lane and consumed inbox items before the audit binding existed, skipping the post-audit tamper guard (consume.go cycle-1506 guard), and almost never fires because core/phase_bindings.go resets the lane to its base after build. The plan's assumption that lanes reach ship committed was wrong.
title: Landing S1 deferred: redesign the pre-scan fast-forward check as a read-only probe, or drop it (console part)
